clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 5, live: 2,000 of the model vectors (seed 381128_05) by eth_call with state override to one endpoint per client release, bracketed by web3_clientVersion.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I queried web3_clientVersion myself: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com answered reth/v2.11.0-b9abbcc/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and https://public-eth.nownodes.io answered Geth/v1.17.10-stable-1df30b18/linux-amd64/go1.27.3. I then ran 13 edge vectors of my own on both endpoints by eth_call with a code override (SDIV and SMOD of -2^255 by -1, MULMOD with modulus 2^256-2, 2^128+1 and 2^192-1, ADDMOD with modulus 2^256-3, SIGNEXTEND at byte 0 and 30, SAR by 255 and 256, EXP 3^(2^256-1), BYTE 31, DIV by 2^128). All 26 results equal the Python reference. The work file out/live.json records the erigon endpoint refusal. That means erigon 3.8.2 was tested from its binary only, as the item says.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 3: jump destination analysis of each binary on the PoolManager runtime (24,009 bytes): 610 destinations accepted and 29 JUMPDEST bytes inside push data rejected.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I fetched the PoolManager runtime with eth_getCode at 0x000000000004444c5dc75cB358380D2e3dE08A90 from https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com and got 24,009 bytes. My own scan that skips PUSH data finds 639 0x5b bytes, 610 of them valid JUMPDEST and 29 inside push data, the same counts as the item. The cache descriptions (keyed by code hash) do not open a path for an ordinary account to make the PoolManager's analysis differ, because the PoolManager's code hash is fixed.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 2 handlers and Task 6: no handler, loop, conversion or jump analysis run of geth v1.17.10, erigon v3.8.2 and reth v2.11.0 differs from the specification, so no line of src/ computes or decides anything else on these builds.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I fetched https://raw.githubusercontent.com/erigontech/erigon/v3.8.2/execution/vm/instructions.go. opDiv, opSdiv, opMod and opSmod call the uint256 Div, SDiv, Mod and SMod directly with no power-of-two shortcut, and opExp has only small-base special cases, as the item says. I also fetched https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/v1.17.10/core/vm/interpreter_gen.go. Its header says execUntraced is the tracing-free path and that a PGO profile makes the handler bodies inline into it, which agrees with the structure item. The conclusion holds for arithmetic, comparisons, shifts, byte conversion and jump analysis. It does not cover persistent storage, transient storage or journal revert in these binaries. The PoolManager's lock, delta count, deltas and synced currency depend on those (src/libraries/Lock.sol, NonzeroDeltaCount.sol, CurrencyDelta.sol, CurrencyReserves.sol). The unit's own high-priority lead names that gap, so the item is not wrongly cleared. Its wording 'no line of src/' should be read as limited to the operations that were run.
